transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because I think I’ve gotten to the point where I’m kind of organizing my life around avoiding elevators, and it’s starting to feel ridiculous but also hard to stop.

Like, at my apartment I’ll take five flights of stairs every time rather than use the elevator, even if I’m carrying stuff or running late. And at work, I do training and development stuff, so sometimes I’m supposed to go to different places for workshops, and I actually turned one down because it was in a high-rise and I knew I’d have to deal with the elevator situation. I didn’t really say that was the reason, but it was.

The thing that made me think I should come in was that I’ve also stopped visiting one of my older computer students. His building doesn’t really have a practical alternative to the elevator, and I used to go help him, but now I’ve been avoiding it. I feel bad about that, because it’s affecting other people too, not just me taking extra stairs. So… yeah, that’s basically why I’m here.
Have you ever had a panic attack or felt extreme anxiety while in an elevator or thinking about being in one?

Yeah, I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack exactly, but it feels pretty close in the moment. It can happen really fast, like even before I’m actually inside one. If I’m walking toward an elevator and I hear that kind of clunk when the doors open, my chest tightens right away, my hands get sweaty, and I get this sudden rush of panic.

It’s like my body reacts before I’ve even had time to think, “Okay, this is an elevator, I’m worried about this.” I’ll just suddenly feel like I need to get away from it, and then I start looking for stairs or some other way out of having to get on.
Do you experience similar anxiety or avoidance in situations other than elevators, such as open spaces, crowded places, or being outside the home alone?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the same way, at least.

Like, crowded places aren’t my favorite or anything, but I don’t avoid them like I do elevators. I can go to a busy store, or be outside by myself, or walk around downtown if I need to. Open spaces don’t really bother me either. It’s more like… if there’s an elevator involved, that’s when my brain starts planning escape routes or trying to figure out how many flights of stairs I can reasonably handle.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed that kind of anxiety spreading to being out alone or crowds or anything like that. It feels pretty tied to elevators.
